In a long, fluorescent-white hallway that looks like it could actually be my local rec center, a tall man in a cheap suit is interviewing an amateur boxer. The man in the suit, whose business attire and need to wear sunglasses indoors is a stark contrast to the amateur boxer, a handsome kid politely waiting for his turn to speak. There is probably a pilates class underway down the hall, as the man we could call a sports journalist starts the interview.

“Right now, I'm chillin' out with my man, tell everybody your name.”

The interviewer pushes his 1960's style antique microphone towards the young boxer.

“Adrien Broner.”

“We talked to the guy you were just boxing. Tell everybody what's goin' on.”

“Well... we've been going to tournaments back to back. We've been winning 'em... but we just never been in the same weight class, so today, we was in the same weight class and we fought, but... I thought I won. I really did, I mean... he was a little too slow for me, and I was in-and-out, in-and-out. But, I guess the judges didn't see it my way, so I just gotta take it on the chin and wait for my next fight.”

“So, what do you think about my man, Shawn Porter? You think he the real deal?”

Adrien laughs. “That's my idol, that's my idol! Oh yeah, he the real deal. We've been in a couple of the same tournaments. We won a couple of the same tournaments, too. That's my guy, right there.”

Fast-forward nearly a decade. At the Mayweather Boxing Club in Las Vegas, Adrien Broner is rhythmically hammering the body shield protecting trusted trainer Nate Jones, as a fixated Floyd Mayweather studies his star protege. Much has been said about the relationship between Adrien Broner and his “big bro” Floyd Mayweather. At the moment, Floyd is offering valuable advice from a lifetime of boxing; but realistically, Floyd gives more to Adrien than just experience. To Broner, Mayweather is a source of inspiration, and it goes beyond AB's repackaging of the Money persona. Broner was 11 years old when Mayweather systematically destroyed Diego Corrales; the fight left a huge impression on the young AB, who watched the fight with his teammates while competing in a Silver Gloves tournament. Floyd Mayweather is everything Adrien Broner aspires to be – the poor kid who took nothing and turned it into everything, the hungry child raised in a broken home who prospered despite the odds. The young athlete who fought his way to fame and fortune.

Adrien has almost everything he ever wanted. He has enough money to pay for his diamond watches, in cash. He has enough fame that TMZ and worldstarhiphop regularly feature Adrien on their frontpages. He has an idol to emulate and a blueprint for success in a brutal business. And, he has the talent to make it happen. But if you go back before Adrien Broner was “AB,” there was Shawn Porter, the idol of the amateur boxer at the local rec center and high-school football phenom turned amateur boxer from Akron, Ohio. Under the guidance of his father Kenny, Shawn used his ferocious athleticism to join Rau'shee Warren and Ricardo Williams as one of the most accomplished amateur boxers to ever fight from Ohio. Before the fame and the fortune, that was who Adrien Broner wanted to be. Tonight, Broner has a difficult task in front of him. Can he beat Shawn Porter, who's rough and relentless style spelled doom for a complacent Broner when he fought Marcos Maidana? Can Adrien Broner live up to his idol? Adrien Broner risks everything tonight on NBC.
